source.title: CorrSteer: Generation-Time LLM Steering via Correlated Sparse Autoencoder Features
source.authors: Seonglae Cho; Zekun Wu; Adriano Koshiyama

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened, but the relevant values can be assigned from their layout and accompanying text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests refusal steering with correlated SAE features and intervention, rather than the original harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction and projection ablation.
record.gate_note: The paper adds positively correlated SAE feature directions and reports HarmBench refusal and XSTest over-refusal outcomes. It does not project the original difference-in-means direction out of every layer and position. The reported feature correlations and feature descriptions are not themselves intervention outcomes.
record.test_reason: This is a general SAE steering-method paper (CorrSteer). It never derives or ablates a harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means refusal direction and does not cite the original. Its HarmBench results come from adding many correlation-selected SAE features, mostly not refusal-related (semicolons, worship, food, 'to be'). It reports only its own method's performance against variants and baselines. That is a related but different construct, so it goes under fits_no_version, not as a test of V1 or V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that correlation-selected SAE features, validated by intervention, improve task outcomes, including HarmBench refusal, with lower side-effect ratios than fine-tuning. They also say XSTest over-refusal remains low. Their own sweep shows over-refusal rising to 21.89% at 1.0× and 36.69% at 1.5×, which qualifies that statement.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Pearson-correlated SAE features and their decoder directions, selected from generation-time activations and added during generation. It does not use a harmful-minus-harmless mean residual-stream direction or test its projection ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with feature selection strategy (single global feature versus per-layer/pruned features), coefficient scale, and pooling strategy. In the coefficient sweep, HarmBench refusal and XSTest over-refusal change with scale; the paper reports collapse beyond 1.5×.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding correlation-selected SAE decoder directions across layers during generation raises HarmBench refusal in Gemma-2 2B (46.61 to 66–74) and LLaMA-3.1 8B (0.71 to 16–18). It also raises XSTest over-refusal (2.37% to 21.89% at 1.0×).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be induced by adding outcome-correlated SAE feature directions, not only a difference-in-means direction.

fits_no_version.finding: The single top-correlated SAE feature (CorrSteer-S) does not raise refusal in either model. Multi-layer feature sets do.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For SAE-feature steering, refusal induction needs features across many layers rather than one feature.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Does not test the original direction or its ablation. HarmBench results show substantial seed variability in Gemma-2 2B CorrSteer-P/A (standard deviations 20.20 and 8.84 in Table 1); the coefficient sweep is reported for one seed. Safety outcomes use a small refusal-detection language model. Table 7's HarmBench values and stated percent scale are unclear/inconsistent.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted beyond the 24 extracted results.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction, no directional ablation, no test that removing a direction removes refusal.
No jailbreak mechanism or adversarial training.
No analysis of refusal geometry. The single vs multi-layer comparison concerns feature selection, not refusal dimensionality.
Harm judgment and refusal are not separated.
No transfer of a refusal direction across languages or model variants.

missing.what: CAA (contrastive activation addition, a difference-in-means style steering vector) adapted to generation-time on Gemma-2 2B HarmBench: 43.14 ± 28.95 vs non-steered 46.61. This is a possible difference-in-means addition with no refusal gain, but the contrast sets used are not described, so the link to V1 is uncertain.
missing.versions: V1 (only if the contrast is harmful vs harmless; unclear)

record.verdict_notes: Relation is set to 'discusses' because the study neither tests nor uses the refusal direction. It does not cite the original. The Gemma 'not safety-trained' stage label should be removed: only the LLaMA 8B example is said to lack safety training. Gemma-2 2B-IT is also used, and which Gemma checkpoint underlies the HarmBench rows is not clearly stated. HarmBench uses 108 samples and a DistilRoBERTa refusal classifier. The coefficient sweep is one seed.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the original difference-in-means direction, projection ablation at every layer and position, or whether ablating it removes refusal. Tests addition of selected SAE features and reports refusal and over-refusal outcomes; general capability is represented here only by MMLU.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.

Compares single-feature and multilayer SAE steering outcomes, but does not test affine or cone geometry, nor determine whether refusal is represented by a dominant direction plus additional directions.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.

No cross-language refusal-direction transfer is tested. Cross-task feature transfer is reported, but not transfer of the refusal feature or refusal direction across model variants or base-to-instruct models.
Does not vary how or when refusal is trained.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2 2B, feature addition on HarmBench and XSTest safe prompts
reader_labels.reason: Multilayer CorrSteer-P/A raise the HarmBench refusal score (r2–r3); the coefficient sweep raises refusal on harmful prompts at 0.5×–1.5× (r5–r7) and over-refusal on safe prompts (r10–r12). These results support an addition effect for selected SAE features, not the original difference-in-means direction.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Single-feature steering, high steering scale, and measured capability
reader_labels.reason: The Gemma single-feature HarmBench result shows no gain (r1); 2.0× sharply reduces harmful-request refusal (r8); and MMLU declines at 1.5× and 2.0× (r17–r18), qualifying broad claims of a single effective direction with abilities largely intact.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2 2B and LLaMA-3.1 8B, single versus multilayer SAE feature steering on HarmBench
reader_labels.reason: In Gemma-2 2B, multilayer CorrSteer-P/A improve the HarmBench score while CorrSteer-S does not (r1–r3); in LLaMA-3.1 8B, multilayer variants score above the baseline while the single-feature variant does not (r22–r24). This supports better outcomes from the tested multilayer feature selection, without establishing a geometric account of refusal.
